name: Kettlebell Outside Snatch
description: A single-arm snatch where **the bell never hikes between the legs.** Start from a tight inside rack — elbow in against the ribs — then drop the bell down and OUT around the working-side hip on an outside pendulum arc, and ride that arc straight up to a locked-out overhead catch in one motion. Inside rack in, outside arc out: the launch position sets the path, and a wide or sloppy rack leaves the arc nowhere to start. It stands to the standard snatch exactly as the outside pendulum swing stands to the standard swing — the offset lateral path trades some hip drive for a frontal-plane and anti-rotation demand, so brace the core hard and don't let the torso twist toward the bell. The hips still drive it, not the arm; punch the hand through at the top so the bell rolls onto the back of the forearm rather than banging the wrist. Go light — an overhead ballistic on an unfamiliar path.
